title: Coordinate subgradient minimization on product domains with an independent optimizer radius
summary: A coherent scalar coordinate interface is studied uniformly over public product geometries. The optimizer-distance budget is independent of the domain diameter, and coordinatewise-motion algorithms form a separate view.

description_paragraphs: Given a public compact product domain $D$ and initial point $x_1\in D$, minimize a hidden convex function over $D$. The complexity is uniform over the permitted public geometries, with the algorithm selected after the geometry is known.
task.formulation: Given a public compact product domain $D$ and initial point $x_1\in D$, minimize a hidden convex function over $D$. The complexity is uniform over the permitted public geometries, with the algorithm selected after the geometry is known.

description_paragraphs: The public domain is $$D=\prod_{i=1}^d[\ell_i,u_i],\qquad-\infty<\ell_i\le u_i<\infty.$$ Singleton factors are allowed. There is no bound on $\operatorname{diam}(D)/R_B$.

An instance is a finite convex Euclidean $G$-Lipschitz function $f:D\to\mathbb R$ and one fixed Borel map $g:D\to\mathbb R^d$ such that $$f(z)\ge f(x)+\langle g(x),z-x\rangle,\quad\|g(x)\|_2\le G\qquad(x,z\in D).$$ At boundary points this supporting inequality is relative to $D$.

At least one constrained minimizer satisfies $\frac12\|x^\star-x_1\|_2^2\le R_B^2$. The radius $R_B$ is independent of the size of the product domain. The pair $(f,g)$ is fixed before the private seed is sampled.

description_paragraphs: One query chooses $(x,i)\in D\times\{1,\ldots,d\}$ and returns only the exact scalar $g_i(x)$. All coordinates at a point arise from the same pre-fixed vector $g(x)$. No function values, active labels, full gradients, coordinate minimizers, or off-domain observations are supplied.
The public inputs are $d,G,R_B,\varepsilon,D,x_1$. Projection onto the known product domain and operations on public geometry are free.

Projection onto the known product domain and operations on public geometry are free.

description_paragraphs: Return any measurable feasible point $\widehat x\in D$ determined by the transcript, including an unqueried point or an average of iterates.
output.feasibility: Return any measurable feasible point $\widehat x\in D$ determined by the transcript, including an unqueried point or an average of iterates.

description_paragraphs: The loss is $f(\widehat x)-\min_{z\in D}f(z)$. The requirement concerns worst-instance expected loss over the independent private seed.
metric.base_expression: The loss is $f(\widehat x)-\min_{z\in D}f(z)$. The requirement concerns worst-instance expected loss over the independent private seed.

description_paragraphs: Every scalar coordinate response costs one call. The query cap holds on every seed and every legal response history. Exact centroid and support computations on known models, arithmetic, and storage are uncharged; their computational runtime is not a charged resource.
resource.budget: Every scalar coordinate response costs one call. The query cap holds on every seed and every legal response history. Exact centroid and support computations on known models, arithmetic, and storage are uncharged; their computational runtime is not a charged resource.

components.description: Its accounting convention is stated in the resource paragraphs.

description_paragraphs: Queries, stopping decisions, and the output are measurable functions of the preceding transcript and an instance-independent private random seed. The unknown instance is fixed before the seed is realized. No span, support, zero-respecting, or memory restriction is imposed.
Internal exact-real computation and storage using public inputs and received information are uncharged. The stated budget must hold on every execution path.
The policy family is chosen using the public geometry. Expected error is uniform over all admissible hidden coherent instances, with a pathwise scalar-query cap.

Queries, stopping decisions, and the output are measurable functions of the preceding transcript and an instance-independent private random seed. The unknown instance is fixed before the seed is realized. No span, support, zero-respecting, or memory restriction is imposed.
Internal exact-real computation and storage using public inputs and received information are uncharged. The stated budget must hold on every execution path.

If a query is made, the first query point is $x_1$. Successive actual query points obey $X_{t+1}-X_t\in\operatorname{span}\{e_{I_t}\}$. The output may be any feasible function of the transcript; no prescribed stepsize formula or last-iterate restriction is imposed.
The same worst-geometry expected-error guarantee is required under the stated motion restriction.

regimes.name: Unrestricted scalar queries: moderate
regimes.predicate_text: $d\ge d_0$ and $q_0\le q\le\sqrt d$; $G,R_B>0$ and $q=GR_B/\varepsilon$. $d\ge d_0$, a universal source threshold. The lower bound already holds on the single normalized box $[-1,1]^d$ with $G=R_B=1$. This is a worst-geometry statement, not a lower bound for every product domain. A singleton domain can be trivial. The normalized hard box has $R_B=1$ independently of its diameter, which grows as $\sqrt d$.

relations.description: The fixed narrow-cube profile ties the feasible circumradius to R. Here the product domain and the nearby-optimizer radius are independent, and the complexity takes a worst case over public product geometries.

objects.definition: Given a public compact product domain $D$ and initial point $x_1\in D$, minimize a hidden convex function over $D$. The complexity is uniform over the permitted public geometries, with the algorithm selected after the geometry is known.
